title: Your Name — Built the old way
tagline: Built the old way. Helped by the new one.

chapters.label: The Bench
chapters.headline:
Built the old way.
Helped by the new one.
chapters.body: I'm a full-stack engineer. I write TypeScript on the edge, ship data pipelines, and read every line before it merges. The assistant drafts. The craft is still mine.

chapters.label: The Foundations
chapters.headline:
Cut by hand,
square on every side.
chapters.body: A computer science degree, then years of TypeScript, React, edge functions and Postgres. The stack changes. Knowing why a query is slow does not.
items: Cloudflare Workers · D1 · Durable Objects · Convex

chapters.label: The Day Job
chapters.headline:
Every panel fitted
by the people who drew it.
chapters.body: Describe your current role here: what you own, who depends on it, and what you shipped.
items: A system you own end to end

chapters.label: The Side Bench
chapters.headline:
Small tools,
no dependencies.
chapters.body: Evenings go to tools I wanted to exist. Most are one file. None phone home.
items: A system monitor in one file, read straight from the kernel
A menu-bar timer that interrupts you with one stretch
A now-playing pill that drops from the menu bar
A game-night scoreboard: one HTML file plus one Worker
A local search over my own notes, indexed into pgvector

chapters.label: The Method
chapters.headline:
I draw the plan.
The apprentice drafts.
chapters.body: Every feature starts as a written design. The assistant writes the first pass. I read it, cut what isn't needed, and the tests decide what merges. Nothing ships that I couldn't have written myself, it just ships sooner.
items: Read every line, delete most of the cleverness

chapters.label: The Road
chapters.headline:
It starts.
It runs.
chapters.body: If you're building something that has to work for years, not weeks, I'd like to hear about it.

chapters.label: Questions
chapters.headline:
Asked before
we start.
chapters.body: The short answers. The long ones are a call away.

qa.a: Full-stack products on TypeScript: React front ends, Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects on the edge, Postgres or D1 underneath, and LLM features where they earn their place.

qa.q: How do you use AI in the work?
qa.a: As the apprentice. I write the design, it drafts, I read every line, and tests decide what merges. Nothing ships that I could not have written myself.
Remote, with overlap for US time zones. On site for kickoffs when it helps.
Open to full-time roles and to well-scoped contracts. Reply within a week, always.
